SectionExerciseRoutes.SourceMathematicsScope: Function, input, output and one-to-one definitions; reasoning is human-reviewed.
Classify explicit and implicit relations using domain restrictions and branch selection.
Substitutions f(a+h), symbolic quotients, all valid inputs and restrictions.
Original plotted curves, graph scales, vertical and horizontal line tests.
Function classification from ordered pairs and tables; no graph-interaction claim.
Look up output and solve inverse table lookup for all listed inputs.
Compute function values and interpret algebraic input substitutions.
Viewport scales and graphical ranges; not an arithmetic substitute.
Applied input-output modeling with units and one-to-one justifications.

SourceExerciseContracts.OriginalMathematicsSourceReview: A relation is a set of ordered pairs; a function assigns every domain input exactly one output.
An input is the independent argument; an output is its uniquely assigned dependent value.
Vertical-line test: more than one intersection gives two outputs for the same x and is not a function.
To test one-to-one, compare whether two distinct permitted inputs share an output.
Horizontal-line test: more than one intersection means the function is not one-to-one.
Not a function: input a has distinct outputs b and c.
Function: distinct inputs a,b,c have one output each (repeating the output c is allowed).
Function: 5x+2y=10 uniquely defines y=5−(5/2)x for every real x.
Function: y=x² assigns one output to each real x; not one-to-one over all reals.
Not a function of x: x=y² admits both y=√x and −√x when x>0.
Not a function of x: 2x+y²=6 has y=±√(6−2x) at many x≤3.
Function: y=−2x²+40x is a polynomial, hence one output per x.
Function: y=1/x for x≠0; x=0 is excluded from domain.
Function: x=(3y+5)/(7y−1) rearranges to y=(x+5)/(7x−3) for x≠3/7; check source denominator y≠1/7.
Not a y-function of x: x=√(1−y²) is the right semicircle; at 0≤x<1 there are two y values.
Function: y=(3x+5)/(7x−1), uniquely defined for x≠1/7.
Not a y-function: x²+y²=9 has two y values at x=0.
Function: x=y³ gives unique real y=cuberoot(x).
Function: y=x³ has one output per real x.
Function: y=√(1−x²), domain −1≤x≤1; principal nonnegative root is unique.
Function: x=±√(1−y) is equivalent to y=1−x²; every real x has one y.
Not a y-function: y=±√(1−x), for x<1 there are two distinct y values.
Not a y-function: y²=x² gives y=±|x| at every nonzero x.
Function: y³=x² gives unique real y=cuberoot(x²)≥0.

SourceExerciseContracts.SourceGraphDescription: Right-opening sideways parabola with two arms from the origin. A vertical line to the right of the origin meets upper and lower branches.

SourceGraphMathParts: Every allowed nonzero x has one output; the asymptote is not another branch.
SourceExerciseContracts.SourceGraphDescription: Reciprocal-like hyperbola with branches in quadrants I and III and the y-axis as a vertical asymptote. There is no plotted point at x=0.

SourceGraphMathParts: Each x has one plotted y, including transition points.
SourceExerciseContracts.SourceGraphDescription: Single connected piecewise rule: negative horizontal left ray, increasing middle line, positive horizontal right ray. Segments meet without contradictory outputs.

SourceGraphMathParts: A vertical line through its interior intersects the upper and lower ellipse arcs.
SourceExerciseContracts.SourceGraphDescription: Small closed ellipse below and to the right of the origin.

SourceExerciseContracts.SourceGraphDescription: Single increasing S-like curve that becomes nearly horizontal around y=0 but never doubles back horizontally.

SourceExerciseContracts.OriginalMathematicsSourceReview: FAILS the vertical-line test: overlapping x-domains of two horizontal rays yield two y-values at x=1.
SourceGraphMathParts: For x=1, the plotted relation has BOTH y≈3 and y≈−3. It FAILS the vertical-line test despite the rays being spatially separated.
